newsitem.title: UK: Amex, NatWest agree credit card deal.
newsitem.headline: Amex, NatWest agree credit card deal.

text.p: National Westminster Bank will issue credit cards that operate on American Express Co.'s global merchant network in a new strategic partnership, the companies said Tuesday.
The deal combines NatWest's strength as a mass-market card issuer with American Express' global merchant network.
The cards will carry the NatWest name and logo as well as the Amex symbol and will be launched in 1997 both for personal and corporate accounts.

In the United States, NatWest plans to issue a United Airlines corporate card that also operates on the Amex system. The card, to be launched next year, will be marketed to large and medium-sized U.S. companies and will act as a cost control tool for corporate travel expenses.

"NatWest is at the leading edge of card development and this new partnership strengthens our commitment to providing innovative card products," said Patrick Boylan, NatWest UK's managing director for card services.
Jonanthan Linen, vice chairman of Amex, said the deal was a major step in Amex's plan to open its network to other card issuers and providing choice to banks and customers.
A personal credit card will be offered in Britain through Natwest and retailers.
